There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
This is a view rather than a table. A view is always treated as read only in the system.

The Type of data Replication determines the directon of the data replication.
Reference means that the data in this system is read only ->
Local means that the data in this system is not replicated to other systems -
Merge means that the data in this system is synchronized with the other system <->

Validation elements: (Space) any character _ Space (fixed character) l any Letter a..Z NO space L any Letter a..Z NO space converted to upper case o any Letter a..Z or space O any Letter a..Z or space converted to upper case a any Letters & Digits NO space A any Letters & Digits NO space converted to upper case c any Letters & Digits or space C any Letters & Digits or space converted to upper case 0 Digits 0..9 NO space 9 Digits 0..9 or space Example of format "(000)_000-0000"

The Maximum Value indicates the highest allowable value for a field

The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.
The key column must also be display sequence 0 in the field definition and may be hidden.
The Parent checkbox indicates if this column is a link to the parent table.
Define button works as action and It will move focus to other tab as per the tab index number defined in field "Tab Index" on Field Tab.

Display encryption (in Window/Tab/Field) - all characters are displayed as '*' - in the database it is stored in clear text. You will not be able to report on these columns.
Data storage encryption (in Table/Column) - data is stored encrypted in the database (dangerous!) and you will not be able to report on those columns. Independent from Display encryption.

Display hashing (in Screen/Tab/Field): All characters will appear as random alphanumeric values. The actual data is stored in a hashed format in the database. These columns will not be available for reporting. Data storage hashing (in Table/Column): This is a one-way process. Once the data is hashed, it cannot be reverted to its original form.
The column must have a value for the record to be saved to the database.
The user must enter a value for this field. The Information is defined in the column and can be overwritten in the Field.
If the field is not mandatory in the database, you can define logic when the user is required to enter a valid value.
The Updateable checkbox indicates if a field can be updated by the user.
If selected and if the winow / tab is not read only, you can always update the column. This might be useful for comments, etc.

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value} or @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@
@Name@>J
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)

Use callout for data entry consequences. The underlying Business Locic class of the table (e.g. MComversionRate.java for table C_Conversion_Rate) has a method "public void set<ColumnName> (String oldValue, String newValue)" (example for column MultiplyRate: setMultiplyRate). This is independent from an explicit external callout.
Use a Callout for data entry consequences. Use the preferred callout method if possible. You need to implement the interface VAdvantage.Model.CalloutInterface.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

You can enter simple logic using variables like @Created@=@Updated@, which fires, when a record is created. If you need to evaluate also values of other records, you need to use SQL logic and need to prefix this logic with "SQL=". Example: start a Order verify workflow, when a business partner ordered something and is over the credit limit "SQL=EXISTS (SELECT * FROM C_BPartner bp WHERE C_Order. C_BPartner_ID=bp. C_BPartner_ID AND SO_CreditUsed > SO_CreditLimit)". Note that the SQL based logic checks for duplicate workflows (i.e. a workflow is started only once per record).

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Mail Template indicates the mail template for return messages. Mail text can include variables. The priority of parsing is User/Contact, Account and then the underlying business object (like Request, Dunning, Workflow object).
So, @Name@ would resolve into the User name (if user is defined defined), then Account name (if Account is defined) and then the Name of the business object if it has a Name.
For Multi-Lingual systems, the template is translated based on the Account's language selection.

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value} or @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@
@Name@>J
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

The relative weight allows you to adjust the project cycle report based on probabilities. For example, if you have a 1:10 chance in closing a contract when it is in the prospect stage and a 1:2 chance when it is in the contract stage, you may put a weight of 0.1 and 0.5 on those steps. This allows sales funnels or measures of completion of your project.

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value} or @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@
@Name@>J
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)
If the field is displayed, the field Display Logic will determine at runtime, if it is actually displayed
The Sequence indicates the order of elements

The Record Sort No indicates the ascending sort sequence of the records. If the number is negative, the records are sorted descending. Example: A tab with C_DocType_ID (1), DocumentNo (-2) will be sorted ascending by document type and descending by document number (SQL: ORDER BY C_DocType, DocumentNo DESC)

The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients. Tenant is a synonym for Client.
An organization is a unit of your Tenant or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

A search key allows you a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).
The name of an entity (record) is used as an default search option in addition to the search key. The name is up to 100 characters in length.
A description is limited to 255 characters.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
The Centrally Maintained checkbox indicates if the Name, Description and Help maintained in 'System Element' table or 'Window' table.

The records are ordered by the value of this column. If a column is used for grouping, it needs to be included in the sort order as well.

The Record Sort No indicates the ascending sort sequence of the records. If the number is negative, the records are sorted descending. Example: A tab with C_DocType_ID (1), DocumentNo (-2) will be sorted ascending by document type and descending by document number (SQL: ORDER BY C_DocType, DocumentNo DESC)
Grouping allows to print sub-totals. If a group changes, the totals are printed. Group by columns need to be included in the sort order.
Before printing this item, create a new page
Calculate the Sum (Σ) of the data if the field is numeric, otherwise total sum length of the field.
A running total creates a sum at the end of a page and on the top of the next page for all colums, which have a Sum function. You should define running total only once per format.
Calculate the total number (№) of not empty (NULL) elements (maximum is the number of lines).
When you want to print running totals, enter the number of lines per page after you want to create a running total line and page break. You should define running total only once per format.
Calculate the Minimum (↓) of the data if the field is numeric, otherwise minimum length of the field.
Calculate the Maximum (↑) of the data if the field is numeric, otherwise maximum length of the field.
Calculate the Mean (μ) of the data if the field is numeric, otherwise calculate the average length of the field.
The Variance (σ²) is the a measure of dispersion - used in combination with the Mean (μ)
The Standard Deviation (σ) is the a measure of dispersion - used in combination with the Mean (μ)

The ID Range allows to restrict the range of the internally used IDs. If selected (excluded), the role cannot access the data specified. If not selected (included), the role can ONLY access the data specified. Exclude items represent a negative list (i.e. you don't have access to the listed items). Include items represent a positive list (i.e. you only have access to the listed items).
You would usually not mix Exclude and Include. If you have one include rule in your list, you would only have access to that item anyway.

If you restrict Access to the entity, you also cannot Report or Export it (i.e. to have access is a requirement that you can report or export the data). The Report and Export rules are further restrictions if you have access.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Mail Template indicates the mail template for return messages. Mail text can include variables. The priority of parsing is User/Contact, Account and then the underlying business object (like Request, Dunning, Workflow object).

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Meta Robots Tag define on how a search engines robot should handle this page and the following ones. It defines two keywords: (NO)INDEX which defines whether or not to index this content and (NO)FOLLOW which defines whether or not to folow links. The most common combination is INDEX,FOLLOW which will force a search robot to index the content and follow links and images.

Define the method how the next occurance is calculated
The frequency type is used for calculating the date of the next event.
The frequency is used in conjunction with the frequency type in determining an event. Example: If the Frequency Type is Week and the Frequency is 2 - it is every two weeks.

The scheduler targets to start the process at the targeted hour/minute and the interval after that. The target hour is in 24 hour (17:00 is 5 PM) of the local system time. Example: Target Hour: 02 - Minute: 00 - Interval: Hour Frequency: 7 The target start date of the scheduler would be 02:00, 09:00, 16:00, 23:00 and then next dat at 02:00 ... If the target hour and minute is 0, this is ignored and only the interval is used to determine the next run.
Minute from 0 to 59 of the process to start

If selected, the process is run only within the tolerance of the specified time - i.e. if it should run Wednesday at 14:00 and the tolerance minutes is 30, the process will not be run if the application server is not available from 14:00 to 14:30.
The toleance in Minutes if the process can run only at the specified time.

If defined, the process runs only of the IP address of the computer matches the IP address defined. Example: You defined 10.10.10 - it will run on all IP addresses, which have this as part of the computer address - including 99.10.10.10 or 10.10.10.99

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

Indicates products that are usually not kept in stock, but are purchased whenever there is a demand. For such products the WMS allocation process will await the receipt of goods through an associated Purchase Order before allocating material for the corresponding Sales Order Line.

Indicates product cost is to be calculated using the Cost Rollup process using pre-defined Routing and Bill of Materials. If the flag value is set to No, then the cost of the product will not be re-calculated in the cost rollup process. Else the cost of the product will be re-calculated in the cost rollup process using the Routing, Bill of Material and current costs of components, resources and overeheads associated with it.

The Guarantee Days is used to calculate the Guarantee (Good until) Date. If the number of trial phase days is not zero, a Trial Asset will be created and the Guarantee Date is calcaulated based on the Trial Phase Days. If the trial days are 0, an asset must exist.

Indicated the origin of the lead or request - might be used in parallel to Campaign or the Self Service flag.

The product is excluded from generating Shipments. This allows manual creation of shipments for high demand items. If selected, you need to create the shipment manually. The Mail Template indicates the mail template for return messages. Mail text can include variables. The priority of parsing is User/Contact, Account and then the underlying business object (like Request, Dunning, Workflow object).
So, @Name@ would resolve into the User name (if user is defined defined), then Account name (if Account is defined) and then the Name of the business object if it has a Name.
For Multi-Lingual systems, the template is translated based on the Account's language selection.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

format := {expression[logic]} ? {cssStyle} [,]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
cssStyle:= {color,background,font-style}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
seprator:=, Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER ? color:red;background:yellow;
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@? color:red
@Name@>J ? color:blue
@Age@>50?color:red,@Age@>20?color:blue
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)
Font Color of item
Define the font size of the item.

The Document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed between greater than and less than symbols
If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field is empty if you create a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).
